## Overview

This integration brings **NS**, the Dutch railways, into Gladys. It gives the **next trains in real time, with their delay and their platform**, at the stations you choose (three in the form, up to 10 more with a button), filtered by train type and direction. It also follows the **disruptions** about each station: incidents (signal failure, broken-down train), engineering works and calamities (storm, strike). Each station becomes a device to show on a dashboard and to use in scenes.

The data come from the **official API of NS** (`gateway.apiportal.ns.nl`), with your own free key. Each followed station is read with one request, every minute by default (every 10 minutes while no station announces a train in the next half hour, at night). The disruptions are read every 5 minutes. The list of the stations of NS is kept by the integration and read again once a week. NS allows 300 requests per 5 minutes per key: the integration always stays below.

NS gives the **expected time** of each train: the delay is the gap with the planned time. **Platform changes** and **cancelled trains** are shown. Station names, messages and disruptions stay in English, as NS writes them.

This is a **cloud** integration: it contacts `gateway.apiportal.ns.nl` with your key. Nothing else leaves your network.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.3.0 or later.
- A free key of the NS API: create an account on [apiportal.ns.nl](https://apiportal.ns.nl/), open **Products**, subscribe to **Ns-App** (free), then copy the **primary key** shown in your profile.

## Configuration

| Field                   | What to type                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API key                 | The primary key of your "Ns-App" subscription (32 characters).                                           |
| Station 1, 2, 3         | The code of the station ("UT", "ASD", the codes of the NS boards) or its name ("Utrecht Centraal").      |
| Train types             | Only these trains: "IC", "SPR", "IC \| ICE". Empty: every train.                                         |
| Direction               | Only the trains going to, or calling at, these stations: "Amersfoort \| Zwolle". Empty: every direction. |
| Reading of the stations | Every 30 seconds, minute, 2 minutes or 5 minutes.                                                        |
| Language of the texts   | Names of the devices, summaries and outputs of the scenes. NS texts stay in English.                     |

The **Find a station** button gives the stations holding a few words, with their code ("Den Haag Centraal [GVC]"). A name works too ("Utrecht", "Den Bosch"); when two stations share it, type the full name or the code. **Test the connection** checks the key and reads each station right away.

The **direction** looks at the destination and at the stations the train calls at next: "Amersfoort" keeps the Intercity to Zwolle that stops at Amersfoort.

More stations than the three of the form (home, work, school…): **Add a station** takes the same three fields — station, train types, direction — and follows up to 10 more stations. **List the stations** shows every followed station, numbered; **Remove a station** takes that number (or the name). The added stations are kept in the configuration of Gladys, so they follow its backups.

## Usage

### Devices

In the **Discover** tab, create the devices you want, **NS \<station\>**:

- the next train as text ("IC 3529 → Venlo · 11 min (+8 min late) · platform 15 (changed)");
- the wait of the next train and of the one after (minutes), and the delay of the next one (minutes);
- the traffic as text ("Disrupted: Utrecht - Amersfoort: fewer trains") and the number of disruptions under way.

At night, without any train, the waits keep their last value.

### Disruptions

NS publishes three kinds: **disruptions** (incidents), **engineering works** (planned) and **calamities** (national messages). The state of a station is the most serious one under way: normal service, engineering works, disrupted or major disruption. Works starting in the next three days are shown as coming.

### Dashboard widgets

![The NS departures widget of Utrecht Centraal and the NS disruptions widget of two stations (generated illustration, not a screenshot)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/William-De71/gladys-nederlandse-spoorwegen/main/docs/assets/widgets.en.png)

- **NS departures**: the departure board of a station: one row per train, with its planned time, its type, its destination, its delay ("+8") and its platform. The row turns orange when the train is 5 minutes late or more or changes platform, red when it is cancelled. The **Trains shown** setting sets the number of rows. Choose a followed station, or type any station (and train types) in the widget settings. With **Several stations**, one widget shows several station devices.
- **NS disruptions**: the state of your stations, then the disruptions and works under way and coming, with their period. Tap a card for the full text. With **Whole network**, the disruptions of the whole Dutch network.

### Scenes

Triggers, once per change (the first reading is only a baseline):

- **NS: train leaving soon**: a train of a followed station leaves in 2, 5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 minutes, counted on its expected time.
- **NS: train cancelled**: a train of the next two hours at a followed station is cancelled.
- **NS: train delayed**: the delay of a train of the next two hours reaches 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes (the highest mark reached). Tick 5, 10, 15 and 30 for any delay of 5 minutes or more.
- **NS: platform changed**: a train of the next two hours leaves from another platform.
- **NS: disruption at a station**: a disruption, works or a calamity about a followed station begins.
- **NS: disruption over**: it is over.

Each gives a ready-made sentence, `{{triggerEvent.data.summary}}`, and its values (train, destination, time, platform, delay, title, cause…). The actions **NS: next trains** and **NS: disruptions of a station** return the same kind of values, to put in a message or to test in a condition.

Examples:

- When the Intercity to Amersfoort leaves Utrecht Centraal in 10 minutes → turn the hall lamp green.
- When your train is cancelled, 15 minutes late or moved to another platform → send the summary to your phone.
- Every weekday at 7:30 → read the next trains of your station and have the kitchen speaker announce them.

### Transport

Cloud only: the data come from the internet. Only the stations you follow are asked to the API of NS, one by one.

## Troubleshooting

- **"NS refuses the API key"**: check that you copied the primary key of the **Ns-App** product, and that the subscription is active on apiportal.ns.nl.
- **"Unknown or ambiguous"**: use **Find a station**, then copy the exact name or the code.
- **"Too many requests to NS"**: the key is shared with another application, or too many stations are read every 30 seconds; choose a longer reading interval.
- **No train**: at night the network sleeps; the station is read every 10 minutes.
- **"NS cannot be reached"**: the integration tries again at each reading; the last trains stay on the widgets.
- **To report a problem**: press **Diagnostic**, then copy the lines starting with "NS diagnostic" from the Logs tab into a GitHub issue or a reply on the forum, with the versions of Gladys and of the integration. The key is never written there.

Fill in your stations, save, then press "Test the connection". |

| Station | `string` | No |  |
| Train types | `string` | No | Empty for every train. |

| Station | `string` | No |  |
| Train types | `string` | No | Empty for every train. |

## How to install Nederlandse Spoorwegen in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Nederlandse Spoorwegen appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/william-de71/gladys-nederlandse-spoorwegen:0.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-nederlandse-spoorwegen](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-nederlandse-spoorwegen).

Nederlandse Spoorwegen requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Nederlandse Spoorwegen is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [William-De71](https://github.com/William-De71), not by the Gladys core team.
